applicationMap.webglNotSupported:
The Instana user interface contains 3D components that are rendered using a technology called WebGL. Unfortunately this technology is not yet available on all platforms. Some browsers, especially browsers in older versions, do not support WebGL. We recommend using the newest generation of auto-updating browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari 8 or MS Edge.

We try our best to support all platform and browser combinations. However, it may be that our usage of WebGL contains errors. You can use an [online test](https://get.webgl.org/) to check whether your platform supports WebGL.

Should the online test state that your platform supports WebGL, but the Instana 3D Map still remains inoperable, [please contact us](https://support.instana.com/hc/en-us/requests/new).

For further troubleshooting information please refer to the [WebGL compatibility table](http://caniuse.com/#feat=webgl) or the [WebGL website](http://webgl.org/).
applicationMap.webglNotInitialized:
You browser supports WebGL, but it can't be initialized. This can happen for some browser and hardware reasons. Some possible reasons are:

  - too many open tabs
  - lack of a dedicated GPU or a busy GPU
  - browser / hardware incompatibility

For further troubleshooting information please refer to the [WebGL test site](https://get.webgl.org/) or the [official WebGL documentation](https://www.khronos.org/webgl/wiki/FAQ).

serviceTroubleshooting.alternativeServicesExplanation:
The current service and its alternative services receive calls which share the same property: same destination host name, same HTTP "Host" header, same infrastructure reference, etc.

For example, the current service receives calls whose HTTP "Host" header is mycompany.com, but it happens that some other services receive calls whose HTTP "Host" header is mycompany.com.

For HTTP calls, the "Host" header is an important piece of information because it is used as the first level cache key in resilient service mapping.
serviceTroubleshooting.alternativeServicesOk: <bold>Is it ok to see alternative services?</bold>
serviceTroubleshooting.alternativeServicesProblem: <bold>No</bold>, if the name of the current service comes from the HTTP "Host" header (service mapping rule whose id is call.http.host) and the name of the alternative service does not (because its name comes from a rule which is based on infrastructure tags), or vice versa. These are duplicate services.
serviceTroubleshooting.alternativeServicesPossibleProblem: <bold>Maybe</bold>, if the current service and the alternative service names do not come from the HTTP "Host" header, then they are either services sitting behind a proxy (good) or they are duplicate services (bad): some of the services are fully linked to infra, while others are partially linked to infra.
